channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: OpenAI quietly lists gpt-rosalind-discovery on its API pricing page — the Rosalind life-sciences line is becoming a family
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: An unannounced gpt-rosalind-discovery model appeared on OpenAI's API pricing page under 'Life sciences models' at the same $5/$25 rate as gpt-rosalind-research — the clearest sign yet that Rosalind is becoming a model family.

item.title: UnionTech's Quick AI turns 3D-printing tribal knowledge into Process Agents: initial plans in minutes, not days
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Shanghai's UnionTech detailed its Quick AI enterprise agent OS today: bespoke "Process Agents" compress initial 3D-print process planning from hours or days to minutes, mining a repository of nearly 5 million archived part models.

item.title: Write an interactive novel with an AI that can't rewrite its own characters: hands-on with AI Novel Studio
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: AI Novel Studio (weike-zhang/ai-novel-studio, MIT) is an AI interactive-fiction app in Next.js + Go where the model proposes each turn's prose and state changes, but the server validates and commits them — so an LLM can't silently rename your characters. Roughly 225 stars in its first week.

item.title: Encrypted AI compute goes on sale in Texas: Texas Inference opens founding reservations, bets businesses — not households — will foot the $3.7T buildout
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Austin’s Texas Inference opened founding reservations today for encrypted AI compute — dedicated model lanes and B300 GPUs that keep data encrypted while it runs. Founder Cooper Scanlon is also making an economic case: the $3.7 trillion in annual revenue the AI buildout needs by 2032 will come from businesses reallocating wage budgets, not consumers.

item.title: You build, AI writes: learn to code while Claude Code builds — hands-on with VibeWise
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: VibeWise (nykooi1/vibe-wise, MIT) is a plugin for Claude Code and Codex that asks for your approach first and checkpoints every design decision, so you actually learn while the AI writes the code. Around 3,300 stars in its first two weeks.

item.title: Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo: Alibaba's 7B image model generates and edits 2K images in 8 steps — with a research-only license
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Alibaba's Qwen team released Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo on October 9: an accelerated 7B checkpoint that generates and edits images at 2K resolution in 8 denoising steps instead of 40. The weights are downloadable, but the Qwen Research License bars commercial use without a separate deal.

item.title: Wondershare launches Filmora 16: an AI-first video editor that tags your footage, tracks subjects, and reframes 360° video
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Wondershare has launched Filmora 16, a major release built around “Edit as an Expert with Filmora & AI”: AI media analysis with searchable tags, camera tracking, color masks, 360° reframing, and a browser-based AI studio for teams.

item.title: TypeSafe raises $870M at a $7.5B valuation, 24 days after launching Jev — venture’s biggest bet yet on AI that decides instead of writes
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: TypeSafe AI has raised an $870 million Series A at a $7.5 billion valuation, led by Andreessen Horowitz with Sequoia and DCVC participating — 24 days after launching Jev, the non-text model that returns calibrated decisions instead of words, and now claims a third of the Fortune 500 as users.

item.title: Text your own AI assistant: a hands-on guide to Open Instinct
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Open Instinct (mariagorskikh/open-instinct, MIT) is an open-source clone of Instinct: a personal agent you text over iMessage, with its own Linux desktop, app connections, and a six-tier permission system that gates every tool call. Around 280 GitHub stars in its first week.

item.title: A global 10-year pause on AI training is feasible, say 26 Berkeley-led researchers — if we hardwire it into the chips
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: A 26-researcher team led by UC Berkeley scholars has released a 200-page blueprint for an international, mutually verified pause on frontier AI training of at least 10 years — enforced not by promises, but by chips that physically can't train new models.

item.title: Indosat and F5 launch the Intelligence Suite: 300+ AI models in one governed platform for Asian enterprises
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Indosat Ooredoo Hutchison and F5 have launched the Indosat Intelligence Suite, a governed enterprise platform putting more than 300 open and closed AI models behind one interface — with token-to-credit billing, intelligent workload routing, and local Indonesian tiers for data-residency needs.

item.title: BloomX raises $13M: the AI that tells farmers exactly when to pollinate
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Israeli agtech startup BloomX has closed a $13 million Series A to scale its AI-timed robotic pollination — machines that buzz, shake and electrostatically gather pollen for the crops honeybees won't touch, with the timing picked by environmental AI models.

item.title: GMO's 6,000-person Gemini bet: Japan's internet giant rebuilds work around AI agents with Google Cloud
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: GMO Internet Group today launched a joint AI project with Google Cloud, giving some 6,000 employees Gemini Enterprise and Google Workspace — and a mandate to redesign whole business processes around AI agents, not just chat with them.

item.title: Pine AI built a cloud computer for AI agents — structure, not screenshots
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Pine AI today introduced Pine Computer, a cloud computer built for AI agents, now in private beta. Instead of reading the web as pictures, it reads pages as structure — and posts the top checkpoint score on a 106-workflow business benchmark.

item.title: Sabi raises $50M from Khosla to turn a baseball cap into a brain-AI interface
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Khosla Ventures leads a $50 million seed round for Sabi, whose baseball-cap EEG sensors read neural signals through hair to translate imagined speech and intent into AI commands — no surgery, no gel. A prototype debuts at CES 2027.

item.title: Apple licenses Huxe's AI audio tech in a quiet hire-and-license deal with the ex-NotebookLM startup
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: A European Commission filing reveals Apple will hire employees from Huxe, the AI audio startup founded by former Google NotebookLM team members, and take a non-exclusive license to its technology — a quiet deal, not an acquisition.

item.title: See how any app really works: reverse-engineer it with an AI agent — hands-on with REA
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: REA (morluto/rea, MIT) is one MCP server that wires your coding agent to professional reverse-engineering tools — Ghidra, Hopper, JADX — so you can ask how any app feature works and get answers with evidence. 41,000+ GitHub stars, #1 trending today.

item.title: Nextech brings agentic AI to the front desk: Assort Health and EliseAI go 24/7 on patient access
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Nextech announced multi-year partnerships with Assort Health and EliseAI to wire agentic AI into its specialty healthcare platform — two AI patient-access platforms integrated into scheduling and intake, starting with ophthalmology.

item.title: Crypto devs rush to Anthropic's OSS Scanner on day one: Nethermind, ZEUS ask Claude Mythos to audit their code — no human review
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Ethereum client developer Nethermind and self-custodial Bitcoin wallet ZEUS were among the first projects to file for Anthropic's free OSS Scanner — day-one applications for Claude Mythos-generated vulnerability reports sent with no human review.

item.title: Operato AI launches an AI-visibility platform: see what ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Perplexity say about your brand
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Operato AI’s new self-service platform shows where your brand ranks in answers from ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Perplexity — which competitors get recommended instead, and what to fix first.

item.title: Ecosia drops Mistral for open models: Kroll says it's about open weights, not China
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Ecosia founder Christian Kroll told EU-Startups that the Berlin search engine is dropping Mistral as its AI provider in favour of open models — pushing back on the idea that the company is simply swapping French AI for Chinese AI.

item.title: Klarent raises €7.13M seed: the agentic QA startup that lets AI write tests — but never run them
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Klarent — formerly fore ai — has closed a €7.13M seed led by Mosaic Ventures. Its agents use LLMs to author test code but execute it deterministically, betting QA becomes the bottleneck as AI writes more of the world's software.

item.title: Run a private AI wealth manager on your own machine: hands-on with Aurelio
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Aurelio (LosaLosSantos/aurelio-finance, MIT) is a self-hosted wealth-management and financial-planning app with an AI advisor you can talk to: net worth, portfolios, fund look-through, cash flow, and goals — all on your computer. 800+ GitHub stars in its first three days.

item.title: Firmus pulls its A$44 billion ASX float: Nvidia-backed AI-factory builder walks away
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Firmus Technologies has withdrawn its application to list on the ASX, killing what would have been Australia's biggest share-market debut since Telstra. Institutional investors balked at the A$44 billion price tag — 44 times what the Nvidia-backed data centre builder was worth a year ago.

item.title: OpenAI answers its fired safety researchers: a "significant breach of trust"
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: OpenAI's research leaders posted a public response on Friday to the three safety researchers dismissed on October 1, saying an investigation found "a significant breach of trust" — and denying the firings were retaliation for raising safety concerns.
